questions.question: In the figure above, ABCD is a rectangle with length 10 cm and width 6 cm. Points W, X, Y, and Z are the midpoints of the sides. What is the area of the shaded quadrilateral?
questions.figure_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 144 112' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' font-family='system-ui,sans-serif'><rect x='24' y='22' width='70' height='42' fill='none' stroke='#222' stroke-width='1.5'/><polygon points='59.0,22 94,43.0 59.0,64 24,43.0' fill='#ccc' stroke='#222' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='18' y='16' font-size='11'>A</text><text x='59.0' y='16' font-size='11' text-anchor='middle'>W</text><text x='98' y='16' font-size='11'>B</text><text x='98' y='47.0' font-size='11'>X</text><text x='98' y='76' font-size='11'>C</text><text x='59.0' y='88' font-size='11' text-anchor='middle'>Y</text><text x='14' y='76' font-size='11'>D</text><text x='6' y='47.0' font-size='11'>Z</text><text x='59.0' y='104' font-size='11' text-anchor='middle'>10 cm</text><text x='100' y='63.0' font-size='11'>6 cm</text></svg>

solution.exhibit_text:
Since W, X, Y, and Z are the midpoints of the rectangle's sides, the shaded quadrilateral's area is always half the area of the rectangle.

Area of rectangle: \(10\text{ cm}\times6\text{ cm}=60\text{ sq cm}\).

Shaded area: \(\dfrac{1}{2}\times60=30\text{ sq cm}\).

questions.question:
What is the value of the expression shown below?
\[150\left(1-\dfrac{1}{5}\right)^2+14=\]

solution.exhibit_text: Evaluate using PEMDAS. First, subtract inside the parentheses: \(1-\dfrac{1}{5}=4/5\). Square the result: \(\left(4/5\right)^2=16/25\). Multiply by 150: \(150\times16/25=96\). Finally, add 14: \(96+14=110\).

questions.question: The average of five consecutive multiples of 4 is 24. What is the **largest** of these numbers?

solution.exhibit_text:
The average of a set of evenly-spaced numbers equals the median. Since the average of five consecutive multiples of 4 is 24, the median is 24: __, __, 24, __, __.

Adding 4 twice to 24 gives the largest number: \(24+2(4)=32\).

questions.question: Diego took 5 quizzes and earned a mean score of 82 points. If the mean score for the first 4 quizzes was 78 points, how many points did Diego score on the last quiz?

solution.exhibit_text:
Let \(x\) represent the sum of the first 4 quizzes. Since the mean was 78: \(78=\dfrac{x}{4}\), so \(x=312\).

The mean of all 5 quizzes is 82, so if \(y\) is the score on the last quiz:

\[82=\dfrac{312+y}{5}\]
\[410=312+y\]
\[y=98\]

questions.question: On a number line, \(\overline{JL}=\dfrac{3}{10}\). Point K (not shown) is located between Point J and Point L. Which value below is a possible value for Point K?
questions.figure_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 60' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><line x1='12' y1='30' x2='188' y2='30' stroke='#222' stroke-width='1.5'/><path d='M10,26 L4,30 L10,34 Z' fill='#222'/><path d='M190,26 L196,30 L190,34 Z' fill='#222'/><circle cx='30' cy='30' r='3.5' fill='#222'/><text x='30' y='16' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' font-family='system-ui,sans-serif'>J</text><text x='30' y='52' font-size='11' text-anchor='middle' font-family='system-ui,sans-serif'>5 1/2</text><circle cx='150' cy='30' r='3.5' fill='#222'/><text x='150' y='16' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' font-family='system-ui,sans-serif'>L</text></svg>

solution.exhibit_text:
Point J is at \(5\tfrac{1}{2}=5.5\). The distance \(\overline{JL}=\dfrac{3}{10}=0.3\), so point L is at \(5.5+0.3=5.8\).

Point K must be between J and L, so \(5.5<K<5.8\). Of the choices, only \(5.65\) falls strictly in that range.
